tonight.headline: Every seat is filled, and the lineup is already the projection lineup
body: Week 3 hasn't started. ESPN projects you 134.5 to Footballers' 120.1, a 57% win probability. The defence slot was filled at 22:25 last night with the Lions, dropping Coleman as the card said. Nothing on your roster plays tonight.
There's nothing to do until Friday's injury reports. Two things to check then: Warren's shoulder (Tuten covers, same kickoff) and Coker's ankle (expected to play).

case.label: Their lineup
case.body: Footballers start Matthew Stafford because Caleb Williams is doubtful, and Christian Watson plays tonight for Green Bay. Malik Nabers was limited Wednesday with a shoulder he 'popped back in' against the Rams, and Brock Bowers is questionable.

case.label: Where you could lose it
case.body: Your 14-point edge assumes Warren plays. If he sits and nobody moves Tuten in, the slot scores zero and the margin drops to about 0 — the Week 1–2 pattern of losing games in the lineup.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Nabers and Bowers both practise fully on Friday. Then their projection goes up by a few points and this is closer to a coin flip than 57% suggests.

tonight.caseSources: ESPN league file · Steelers.com · Giants.com · Bleacher Report

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — check Friday's Steelers report; both kick off Sunday 11:00
doFirst.title: Only if Pittsburgh rule Warren out: start Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: Unarmed. Don't fire this today. Warren starts unless Friday's report lists him OUT or DOUBTFUL.

case.label: The evidence so far
case.body: Warren was limited Wednesday with the shoulder (Steelers.com, NBC). Limited is still practising. Dowdle didn't practise and wore a walking boot; Rapoport calls him day-to-day (Yardbarker). If Warren plays he has the backfield.

case.label: Why a card and not a note
case.body: This is the Pitts lesson: a startable back-up on the bench goes on a card, not in a footnote. Tuten leads Jacksonville's backs in snaps and carries, and Lawrence says they'll 'lean on him more and more' (SI, 24 Sep).

case.label: Why not now
case.body: By projection Warren is 15.0 and Tuten 11.0. Swapping on a 'limited' tag gives up four points for no reason. Both kick off at 11:00 Sunday, so there's no timing trap.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Warren is a full participant Friday. The card then never fires and costs nothing.

action.label: Start Tuten · bench Warren (only if Warren is ruled out)

whatWentWrong.title: Last night's brief said Coker wasn't on the injury report. He was.
whatWentWrong.lead: Limited Wednesday with the ankle, per CBS. It doesn't change his start, but it's a Friday check, not a clean slate.

case.label: What happened
case.body: The 04:40 brief read ESPN's QUESTIONABLE as left over from last week. CBS reported him limited Wednesday. The Athletic's Joe Person says his availability isn't in doubt, and he caught eight passes on the same ankle last week.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing yet. He stays in the flex. If Friday downgrades him, McLaurin (11.9) is next in by projection, then Boston (11.3).

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Carolina list him full on Friday. That would mean Wednesday was maintenance.

worthALook.name: Evan McPherson
worthALook.lead: The kicker comparison, answered hold. The two sources disagree about Pineiro.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: PFN (Katz, 22 Sep) rank McPherson K1 and Trey Smack K4, both free agents here, and Pineiro K17. ESPN has Pineiro 9.4 (K2), Smack 8.7 and McPherson 7.4. PFN's ranks are role-based; ESPN's number is a projection.

case.label: Why hold
case.body: Pineiro came in on 23 Sep, so a move now is a second change to the seat inside a week. And there's no free roster spot without dropping a player you'd rather keep.

case.label: When to act
case.body: 30 September, when the churn window closes — if Pineiro finishes Week 3 outside the top twenty kickers while McPherson or Smack finish top five.

doNotChase.name: Dalton Schultz
doNotChase.lead: The market is right about him and it doesn't matter here.

case.label: The role
case.body: PFN (20 Sep): 14 targets, including a 12-catch, 140-yard game, and he's taking Houston's volume with Nico Collins' hamstring uncertain.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Chem has one tight-end slot, Likely's, and the flex takes RB/WR only. A second tight end scores you zero.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely showing up on a Giants injury report. He isn't on this week's.

doNotChase.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
doNotChase.lead: Plays tonight. The structural reason he's gone doesn't change whatever he scores.

case.label: The fact
case.body: Michael Penix Jr. is listed questionable but expected back tonight at Green Bay (Democrat-Gazette, 24 Sep), so the quarterback case for dropping Pitts is gone.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One tight-end slot, held by Likely; the flex is RB/WR only. In Week 2 he played 26 of 69 snaps, behind two back-up tight ends.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely getting hurt. Separately, the log grades this decline WRONG if Pitts outscores Likely in two of the next three weeks.

doNotChase.name: Jaxson Dart
doNotChase.lead: Still the biggest ownership anomaly on this wire, and ownership is falling fast for a reason.

case.label: The fact
case.body: ESPN report a season-ending knee injury; Jameis Winston starts.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing. You start Josh Allen in a one-quarterback league.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. The sample is thin — two weeks — but the tool's answer stands.

settled.result: Fired within ninety minutes and took the Vikings D/ST with it. That's why today's ghost card starts its title with 'Only if'.

settled.result: Dart is out for the season and Likely isn't on the injury report, so Winston's the settled starter and Likely's the settled TE1.
